utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, what was your personal weapon of the day throughout that time?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I had a sniper weapon. I had a Zolja, a Yugoslav Zolja.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you and your men have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, not all of us had uniforms. Some of them had some signs. I had only a blue bullet-proof velvet and I had only some trousers of the Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about a helmet? Did you have a helmet?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I had a helmet. That is a green helmet of the Yugoslav Army. I was the only one which had such a helmet.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why were you wearing a Yugoslav Army helmet?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There is no connection. We had the weapons of Yugoslav Army, of the Chinese army, all the weapons we could lay hands on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you're recorded as saying: "Not all of us had uniforms. Some of them had signs." By "signs," do you mean patches or something else?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: If you did not have uniform, they wanted to have a -- saying it was the patch of UCK.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying that some soldiers had uniforms, some didn't have uniforms, but everyone had a patch?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No. As I said, this was a voluntary army. We tried to organise ourselves as better as we could, but we did not have a factory or somebody who could produce clothes or uniforms or weapons for us. So we took whatever we could lay hands on. So even if they did not have uniforms, we tried to provide these people a kind of a sign, a patch, so that they could be identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about the military police. Mete Krasniqi, Avni Krasniqi, Iber Krasniqi, and Vesel Dizdari, were they members of the military police unit?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: These were members of the local police in the village of Vranoc, and later the military police from the village of Vranoc after the 3rd Dukagjini Brigade was formed, they went to Barane, they participated there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they then considered to be members of the military police or operating as military police officers?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They were considered like military policemen, simply military policemen, but I don't know what they said when they went to places, how they introduced themselves. But from what we knew, they were members of the military police and they carried out the duties that they were tasked with.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Hasan Gashi, was he under Nazif Ramabaja's command?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: After the police were transferred from the village to the primary school in Barane, we decided to select the best young men from all the villages to make them members of the military police. So we tried to have two people from each village to become members of the military police so that there would be no misunderstanding between the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was Hasan Gashi's role in this?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Hasan Gashi, because he used to work in the Yugoslav police earlier, he was somebody who knew what his task was and he was a member of the military police in Barane.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was he under Nazif Ramabaja's command?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, we tried to have a brigade commander who could give clear instructions and who would be somebody who knew what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Was he under Nazif's command?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He was under Nazif's command, but to what extent he carried out the orders, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to go over the training you provided the young soldiers. Now, you had been a professional police officer. Did you train them in the use of weapons, including rocket-launchers and anti-aircraft guns?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many young soldiers did you have under your training?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, the number varied. It was never the same. When I started, there were 21 of them, but the number went up to 700, 800, or even a thousand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said before that there was a shortage of uniforms. What about weapons? Were there enough weapons to go around for these up to 700, 800, or even a thousand soldiers you trained?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, we did not have enough weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you able to say now what percentage of soldiers had weapons and what didn't? 10? 20? 30? 50? 80? Whatever?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, where I was and from what I could see in the primary school in Barane, it could be 50/50, and we tried to share those weapons. If we heard of an attack somewhere, we had to use the same weapons to go to that place to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying you shared weapons?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just on the issue of uniforms, the Black Eagles, were they uniformed different to the other KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I heard about the Black Eagles later. In the beginning we heard that they were military police, and the military police, whoever could lay hands on an uniform, they had uniforms, they were black uniforms. Mostly, in fact, they were civilian clothes. It was an attempt for us to have a unit and to work with that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked you about Ramush Haradinaj before and your visiting him in Gllogjan. I want to ask you now about his visiting your brigade in Barane. Do you remember him coming to the oath-taking ceremony on the 20th of July, 1998? Were you there then?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I was there. The date was the 20th of July, 1998, and this was the oath-taking ceremony for new soldiers. It was a solemn event. Ramush came. We were also present. Tahir Zemaj was there. We were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Ramush visit your brigade a couple of -- on a couple of occasions there, accompanied by Sali Veseli and Idriz Balaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Ramush came but Balaj was not with him. I did not see him, he was not there. Sali came on his own and Ramush came on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the oath-taking ceremony in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The aim of the visit was because we had made a request to him. We had a great number of soldiers that wanted to join the KLA and we wanted them to pledge their allegiance and we wanted him to be present in this ceremony so that he could see from close what these young men were doing and how they were so eager to join the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who's the "he"? You're referring to Ramush Haradinaj there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Ramush. We invited him and we wanted him to be part of that solemn ceremony, in the oath-taking ceremony of the new members of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was it so important to you that Ramush participated in this?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: It was important because people loved him. People wanted to see him and to get to know him from close by, because for them, Ramush was an idol and he still is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they see him as a strong, powerful commander?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I appreciate Mr. Re may not be getting the answer that he wants, but to seek to put words into the witness's mouth through the form of leading questions, in our submission, is not an appropriate course. Let him ask the questions in a non-leading form and have the answers that he gets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, could you reformulate the question or put another question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that for people Ramush was an idol. Why did they see him as an idol?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. That's what people thought. They trusted Ramush and they thought that he was a person who sacrificed his own family to protect the whole population, and that's why he was considered an idol. So he was not ready to sacrifice only himself but his whole family.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the feedback you were getting from these people about Ramush's command style?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Ramush had no time to command everywhere, but people trusted him. They thought that if Ramush went there, there would be no problem for them, for the people. This is something that occurred among the people. That's how the people loved him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the FARK and the KLA, what do you see as the -- what was your perspective on what was happening between the FARK and the KLA at the time when Ramush and Tahir Zemaj were at this oath-taking ceremony?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This is a very important question because at that time we were calling upon all officers, former officers, to come and join us so that they could train the soldiers and prepare them. And in Kosova at the time, there was no presence of any other force other than the KLA. Later we heard that there was another force which was called the FARK, but on the ground, we knew only of one force, which was the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was Tahir Zemaj's role? Who did you think he was?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Tahir Zemaj was a professional. He had graduated the military academy, had been a superior officer in the Yugoslav Army. He left the Yugoslav Army and came to help his own people, just like any other officer. He came to make his own contribution and nobody stopped him. And I remember something that Ramush told him, You're welcome. This is your country. Fight for your own country and for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of any differences between Tahir Zemaj and Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Differences -- well, there were differences between us because Tahir had a higher rank, Ramush was much younger than him, and I was younger as well. So he was a superior officer; we were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm talking about antagonism as opposed to physical or age differences.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Physical appearance, no, we didn't pay attention to those things. I remember that Ramush came first, then Tahir came later. We were all together. You have the video-recording of that. We were all together. We were not on different sides. We were all members of the Kosovo Liberation Army without any distinction, because if we had any differences or arguments, we wouldn't have been together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you about is were you aware - and if you're not, just say no - of any personal antagonism, difficulties, or rivalries between Ramush and Tahir?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of anything like that. There might be rivalry everywhere. People might have different opinions, but I don't think there were any such problems there. Of course, each and everyone has his or her own opinion and in democracy you can have a different opinion, but there was no clash. Well, if I did not agree with something that Tahir said or Ramush said, I could have told them and they could have done the same with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't think you're suggesting there was a democracy in Kosovo in 1998. What I'm asking you about is whether there were any fights or clashes between the two.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There were no clashes or fights. There was no clash between them, at least I don't know of any. I'm not aware of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of any military clashes or fights between members of the FARK and members of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a compound and slightly confusing question, military clashes or fights. I don't know whether Mr. Re has in mind any kind of military engagement; but if he does, none of us in this case are aware of any evidence to suggest such a thing. So perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of any physical fights involving weaponry between members of the KLA and the FARK?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, for the time I was there I never heard of anything like that. I heard things after the war, but I don't think they have much weight. At that time I know that we were all together. If there had been any fighting between them, Ramush was with Tahir together in Prapaqan. I did not see anything. Ramush came first, as I said; Tahir came later and there was no clash. I never heard or I never saw any kind of fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A few moments ago you said that people considered Ramush to be an idol and he still is. Is that your view of Ramush?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Of course. If 90 per cent think of him like that, why not me?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As a commander of soldiers, did you give your subordinates any training in the rules of war or how to treat civilians or prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I trained them. I spoke to them every day, one hour each morning, and I spoke to them -- and I told them that, There won't be war forever. One day we will have peace and each and everyone will be held responsible for their actions. For this reason, everybody had to behave properly, to be careful in what they did, not to maltreat civilians, who were numerous and were -- had remained homeless because of the villages that had been burned. There were concentrations of people in various areas, and if they had a prisoner of war or somebody surrendered to them, hands up, these people should not be maltreated. First of all, that person should be given some safety and security, given food and water, and the professionals should deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did that actually happen or is that just theory?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This was the theory that I spoke to them about every day, but we did not have the strength to catch anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about collaborators or suspected collaborators, how were they to be dealt with?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The same as everybody else. If they were suspected, then we had to speak with these people; and in the course of that conversation -- however, I must say here that there were not many people that we suspected to be collaborators. If we could investigate, we tried to investigate, but it was very difficult for us to do these things. We just tried to isolate the person, ask him or her what they had been doing, and after the interrogation they were left free.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask you about one of those. Skender Kuci, did you know him in 1998?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, I did not know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you know his brother, Adem, did you work together in Pristina as police officers before the war?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I knew his brother, he was a police officer, but he used to work in Pristina and I worked in Prizren, and he's still there, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, was Adem brought to you one day when you were in Barane?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he brought to you by KLA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, my soldiers brought him. That day Adem had been seen together with Serb police forces in the Kliqine village where the police station was. It was about 10.00 in the morning and after he had left the police station, he got -- had gotten into his car and had been driving into the direction of the Barane area, towards Qallapek. At that time, the Serbs, even the ill people -- they did not even allow the ill people to go to hospital and get a cure, while they allowed him to move freely. And I was notified that this person had entered our area at 10.00, after he had left the Serb area, and I thought maybe he has a big problem, because it's difficult for the Serbs to leave someone move freely in the area. And he came to me and we talked about his problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he come to you or did the soldiers bring him to you?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, the soldiers brought him to me, but he was not ill-treated or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in their custody or just travelling with them?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: No, he was travelling with them. They just had seen him in the area and had seen him talking to the Serbian police, and they came to me and said, This is a suspicious person. And I said, Wait a minute. You cannot make a judgement on people just like that. First we have to talk to him and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he tell you about his brother, what had happened to his brother, Skender?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: First of all, when he was brought he was a little bit concerned and he did not recognise me, but I recognised him. And I tried to calm him down. I said, You can rest a little while. And I said, What's your problem? Why did you come through the Serb police? Because the Serb police must -- might have killed you, passing in their area, so what's your problem. And he said, This is my problem: A brother of mine has been taken, he must be in your area. I said, I don't know about this case. And he said, No, I know for sure that my brother has been taken and he is in this area. I told him that I have no information about this, but it's not proper for you to go and speak with the Serbs and you could have been killed because people are armed these days.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement of the 15th of May, which you signed in Albanian and English, you said that: "Adem told me that his brother had been captured by the KLA and he was looking for him." Is that what he told you?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you tell him he should make further inquiries of?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He told me that his sister lived in Qallapek and two sons of that household were my soldiers in the area, and I told him, Because your sister lives here, you go and stay with your sister. Take your -- these soldiers and look for your brother with these soldiers. I have no idea about this case. If the soldiers can help you, they will inform you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did he find that his brother was taken to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't know. After I let him go, he left and he did not return to me. So I have no further information.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said in that same statement about two weeks after this you found out that Skender had died. What did you find out or how did you find out that Skender had died?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I did not say I discovered. Somebody informed me that Skender was dead. I did not make inquiries. I asked somebody in Qallapek what happened, did he find his brother. And They told me, Yes, he found his brother. He was dead. That was -- really happened two weeks after he had met with him me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear that he had been died after being detained in KLA custody in --

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: That's a leading question. I would ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: -- if possible, for Mr. Re to ask questions in an open manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There's a reason why I've asked this way --

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- in this form. There's a reason why I've asked the question in this form and it's a credit issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the objection is sustained and I invite the -- I -- Mr. Re, I take it that you have reasons to do what you do but that doesn't mean that it's admissible, and I invite the Defence to be brief in their objections. There was --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a previous one about leading. The further explanations on what Mr. Re was seeking with his questions were superfluous.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I understand that. May I simply raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- what Mr. Re has just said as to his reasoning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- behind the leading question, because my understanding of what he is implying is that he proposes to now seek to impeach his own witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's just wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's fine. If it's a credit issue, perhaps he might explain what he means by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if he just reformulates the question or puts the question in another way, then we avoid further discussions on the matter. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear that he had been detained by KLA --

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- from anyone else --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's not a leading question. He can answer it in any way. He can say, yes, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Re, what is a leading question? A leading question is either a question which -- in which an assumption is included of a fact that has not yet been established or a leading question is a question which already leads the witness to a certain answer. Would you please reformulate your question. Perhaps -- Did you hear anything about how Skender Kuci died, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not hear how. I only heard that he was dead, but not heard how.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you hear where he died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 88 of your statement which is before the Court you refer to: "Sometime before September 1998 I heard about the abduction of the couple Nurija and Istref Krasniqi. Tahir Zemaj called me to Prapaqan to ask if I knew what happened to the couple." I just want to ask you for a little further clarification on that. Were you -- or had you heard anything about suspected collaboration in relation to this particular couple?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that is true, what I said in that paragraph. I was called by Tahir. These people were in the area covered by my command. Tahir then decided to ask me. He thought that I was in the best position to know about this. I went there. I explained to him that I know nothing and -- I knew that one of the sons was injured. We provided assistance. We took the son to the military hospital to get treatment. This is what I think. On the way then there were Serbian forces, and then later I learned that their bodies were brought from Serbia recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In paragraph 89 you said: "I later heard different gossips about their killing. Rumours had it that they were collaborating with the Serbs." If you can, I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what you had heard and who you had heard it from. What were these rumours?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The rumours are rumours. There are rumours every day and everywhere. If you don't see something with your own eyes, then you cannot prove something. I have heard different variants. Somebody said that they were killed, somebody said different thing, so there are many suppositions, many different opinions. So I was not interested any longer to know anymore. Somebody was lying, somebody was giving his own opinion, different variants, these are rumours in the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some photographs and some maps. Now, you marked several maps which were attached to your statement. The first one I want to show you is 65 ter 1027, which is a hand-drawn map which you've marked on Ramush's Gllogjan staff headquarters. It's going to come up on the computer in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be number P352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you see the document in front of you, Mr. Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to tell the Trial Chamber about the diagram you have drawn there. In the statement it's described as a rough sketch of three brigades and how they were located in relation to the staff headquarters in Gllogjan and you've shown on that where Ramush had his staff headquarters from where he commanded the Dukagjini operational zone, particularly the three brigades at Barane, Prapaqan, and Bardhaniq and you signed it. I'm just reading that from paragraph -- between paragraph 9 and 10 of the statement of 5th of March, 2006 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we just pause for a moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- please, and identify those paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's headed investigator's notes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- between --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a comment by an investigator, as I understand it, rather than by the witness. Is that correct? The words that Mr. Re has just put to this witness as his statement are, in fact - I think I'm right, I stand corrected - actually words of an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I didn't say that. I said: "In the statement it's described s as ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Not by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I actually hadn't finished the question, but I'm grateful for Mr. Emmerson's premature interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's keep matters short. If you are quoting from a statement, you -- it would be easily understood as quoting what the person who gave the statement said. Here it clearly is not. Let's avoid further trouble about it, and, Mr. Re, if you put to the witness what it is, please be unambiguous in who said what you are putting to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I actually said I'm just reading from that between paragraphs 9 and 10 and it's headed investigator's notes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Actually, let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- I just read it on to the record a moment ago. I can re-do -- all I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that you are reading that from between paragraph 9 and 10 of the statement of the 5th of May, and I now further clarify that what we find between paragraph 9 and 10 - the witness might have forgotten about it - is a note of the investigator. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's headed investigator's notes and it said you created a rough sketch of the three brigades and how they were located in relation to staff headquarters in Gllogjan and you drew on the sketch that Ramush had his staff headquarters at Gllogjan from where he commanded the Dukagjini Operational Zone, particularly through the gates at Barane, Prapaqan and Bardhaniq, and it's signed by you in the annex as A. The question is this: Is that an accurate description of this particular diagram?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I draw well. I have tried to pin-point the locations of the brigades to the extent that it is possible because you need a lot of time to draw a map; however, I've tried to my best possibilities and these were more or less the locations. You can see also the villages there. This is an accurate map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And is it accurate to say that that is a sketch of where Ramush had his --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What Mr. Re is trying to do is to lead the witness to agree with an investigator's note which contains within it a suggestion that from Gllogjan, Mr. Haradinaj commanded the three brigades. That's the purpose of this leading question, to try to get the investigator's comment on what the witness was trying to convey into evidence through a leading form of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, you are invited to -- not to lead in this respect. And just for clarification, you earlier said to me, and I'll find exactly what you said. At the risk of making a mistake I think you said, this question is not leading because the witness could say yes, the witness could answer by no and the witness could answer by saying that he doesn't know. If I would put a question to someone whether he had had for lunch ravioli with pea soup, then of course the witness could say yes, the witness could say no, and the witness could say I don't know anymore. Nevertheless, this question is highly leading the witness since it suggests that he had ravioli and pea soup for lunch. So therefore, I have some concern about your understanding of what a leading question is, specifically in view of your explanation why the earlier question was not a leading question. Would you please keep that in mind and refrain in this respect from leading. Apart from that, of course the Chamber has seen this map and has some -- at least I had some difficulties with the geography also. So please try to obtain the evidence which assists us. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber may rest assured that I do have a reasonably attuned appreciation to a leading -- it may not have come across that way before but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There will be another moment where we can exchange our views on technical matters of criminal procedure. Let's for this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, just look at the map again. Now, on it you've drawn -- you've written under Gllogjan, Ramush, staff HQ; under Jablanica, Lahi Brahimaj, staff HQ; and you've also drawn on Tahir brigade at Prapaqan; Bardhaniq, Musa brigade; and brigade at Barane under Nazif. What was your purpose in describing Gllogjan as a staff HQ and Jablanica as a staff HQ and the other one as brigades?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This was a request of the investigator. He asked me about the locations. He asked me whether I could make a sketch of them. We had the map; however, he asked me to make a sketch with my hand. I tried to do my best, so I made this drawing. I showed the locations we had at that time. Each of us worked independently because we did not have means of communications. We did not have radio for communications, telephones, there were no telephones in the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you describe Gllogjan and Ramush as the staff HQ on that map?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He asked me to make the sketch and this is what I did. I made the sketch as much as I knew. The headquarters were there in the village of Gllogjan. Then he asked me about the location of the 1st Brigade, of Tahir, and then I made the drawing of Tahir. Then in Bardhaniq was Musa, I also made some kind of sketch and then also showed the route with -- I have not mentioned here, specified all the villages. I have also shown the 3rd Brigade in Barane where I was and also I showed Jabllanice where Lahi was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 31 of your Rule 6 -- sorry, Rule 92 ter statement, you referred to the training of UCK soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, may I just try to seek some clarification. First of all, I take it that you want this annex A to be exhibited and tender it into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the legenda are not translated, so therefore, it's not entirely clear. Also, as I said before, the geography, for example, on this map we find Jabllanice and Gllogjan at approximately the same distance from a road which I have to assume is the road between Decani and Djakovica, whereas, of course, in reality on the real maps you find a totally different picture. So therefore -- but with some imagination you can get an idea of what the witness may have intended to do. But let's explore the matter a little more in detail. You -- on this map I find at two places staff HQ, that is, Gllogjan, Ramush, staff HQ; and Jabllanice, Lahi Brahimaj, staff HQ. Could you tell us staff HQ of what exactly? Could you further explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were local commands. The striped area, these are the rivers. So that's why they might be a little bit confused. So this -- here you can see the Decan river, the striped area, and also the Peje river. Decan is a municipality. Jabllanice is in the municipality of Gjakove. Therefore, this drawing might create some confusion. We could not use coloured pencils. That's why I put so many lines in this area to show the river. This area here with dots and small lines, these are the routes, the route to Prilep, to Irzniq, to Gllogjan. So these are the signs I used for routes with the dots, small lines, and the other one where you can see more lines and darker, that's the rivers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said these are local headquarters, Gllogjan, the same for Jablanica, as I understand. Now, we also find with -- three numbers, brigade. I see one Bardhaniq; one Prapaqan, Tahir; one Barane, Nazif. Are these brigades in any way related or linked to what you just called local headquarters, whether Jablanica or Gllogjan or any other headquarter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could not hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll put the question again to you. I asked: Are these brigades, as we find them, Tahir brigade, Nazif, and Musa, are these brigades in any way related or linked to what you just called local headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This was done in order to raise the morale. We set up three brigades of regular army. We did not have the equipment, the means, and the uniforms. However, this was done for propagandistic reason, to tell the people or to show the people that we have three strong armies located in three separate areas in which young people are engaged. This was the purpose. However, they were, let's say, part of the same brigade but only to raise the morale in the people we showed it as if it was three separate brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's still not entirely clear. For example, let's take one example, Prapaqan, Tahir brigade as we find it on the map, was that in any way linked to either staff headquarters in Gllogjan or staff headquarters in Jabllanice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they were not linked. In Gllogjan there was Ramush, in Prapaqan it was Tahir. Each operated independently, which means that we did not have the means and the possibilities to communicate with each other. However, if there was a problem or if we wanted to send some information, we send a courier in order to ask for some help. When I was in Barane if I had some problems, then I send some soldier with a vehicle in order to ask for help. I sent him to Ramush, to Lahi, or maybe to Tahir, the one which was closer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you apparently make a distinction between what you call brigade and what you call staff headquarters. Could you explain to us what then exactly the difference is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no interpretation again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- I'll try it again. You make a distinction in your description between what you call a brigade and what you call staff headquarters. Could you tell us what the difference is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The difference is that in the brigade we had the officers, the officers -- the purpose was to have as many officers as possible. There were also officers with Ramush. This was how we decided at that time. This is what we did. This was done in order to attract as many officers as possible. The same thing happened also with other brigades in other parts of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That still does not explain why one time you say "staff headquarters" and another time you say "brigade."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The meaning of "brigade" is different from that of the staff. In fact, we did not have a regular army, not a regular unit. The reasons are various, due to logistics, et cetera. I know what a regular army means. A regular army should have the logistic, the officers, the military equipment, everything. So we tried to set up a brigade, in fact, to give a name to something which was not really a brigade. A brigade should have three battalions. A battalion should have up to 1.000 people. A brigade, it's clear, should have up to 3.000 or more people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You now describe brigade as a unit of a certain size. Now, you earlier said a brigade is not the same as a staff. What now is a staff for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The staff at the wartime is a leading structure, a structure which leads the brigade. Therefore, we set up a staff in every village in order to raise the morale of the people. So there was a staff in every village, an army staff. The young people of the village were engaged in that staff to defend the village. This was a local staff. There are several people in the staff which lead the army --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, for Prapaqan and for Barane and for Bardhaniq, you say "brigade," you do not say "staff." Now, why do you use the word "staff" for Jabllanice and for Gllogjan and why don't you put there "brigade" or whatever, "unit"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I told you, staff is a leading structure, that is the purpose. In Gllogjan there were also soldiers, probably more soldiers than the soldiers in the brigades in Prapaqan and Barane. But this is how it was described, and we did not have the right names at the time. People joined several units, and then brigades were set up with different names such as Jusuf Gervalla Brigade and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in Gllogjan and Jabllanice where you said these -- the "leading structure," was the function of the leading structure you called "staff," were they limited to Gllogjan itself and to Jabllanice itself, or did they extend any further than those villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Every village has its own staff. The brigades have their own staffs as well, leading structure. The leading structure of every brigade. In Gllogjan there were many soldiers. There were many soldiers in Jabllanice there as well. This is the character of the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do I then understand that despite the difference in names, that the function of the leading structure was limited to Gllogjan itself and would not extend to any of the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, Gllogjan had its own staff, its own leaders; Prapaqan, its own staff, its own leaders; same with Bardhaniq, as well as Jabllanice and Barane and other villages. I mentioned only a few villages just for your information. However, each village had its own command and its own leaders that led them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What period are we exactly talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are talking about the period of the brigades, that's how they were called on the ground. This is 1998, about June or July of that year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Hoepfel has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Witness, may I ask you an additional question as we have this sketch on the screen you drew in March 2006. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One short question at this moment because we will need a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Just to understand your description, what does the heading on the left upper corner, these three lines, mean? Give an explanation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question here was about the Gllogjan staff, only about that, not including the other staffs. And the question was: Who was the commander of the staff in Gllogjan, and I said Ramush. The operative commander was Sali Veseli and Rrustem Tetaj. These three were the leaders of the staff in Gllogjan. As regards the duties each of them had, I don't know, especially about Rrustem. But I know that they were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: One word if I may. I'm not sure how much longer Mr. Re has in chief with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know, either. Mr. Re, could you already -- I don't know whether we need -- I would like to have a break now quickly, because we are well over time. Mr. Re, how much time you would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: However long it takes me to get the witness to tender one -- six photographs --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and maps but that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All I'm asking is, I'm going to seek Your Honour's permission to begin my cross-examination tomorrow rather than this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give an indication as to how much time you would need for the cross-examination? And I'm now addressing all three counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I would expect somewhere in the region of an hour to an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that would mean there would be no other witness available, Mr. Re. So we would finish tomorrow. May I -- I don't know, Mr. Guy-Smith, Mr. Troop, we would easily finish the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: We will easily finish the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break, with the apologises to transcribers and interpreters. Therefore we'll take a bit more time, ten minutes past 6.00 we'll resume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Re, I'd like to put another few questions to the witness. Mr. Krasniqi, may I put to you some portions of the statement that has been admitted into evidence and I first go to paragraph 33. Your statement in paragraph 33, you could, if you wish, you could follow it in your own language since I do understand that you have a copy in front of you. It says: "The office of Din Krasniqi was located at his house in Vranoc village. He also had a private clinic at this place. In February 1998 not many people had uniforms. Most of them were training in civilian clothes. In February 1998 it was a known fact that an army existed in Jablanica under the command of Lahi Brahimaj. Din Krasniqi had visited Jablanica, and being a trust-worthy person he was allowed to call himself as the commander of the Barane valley." Who allowed Din Krasniqi to call himself the commander of the Barane valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this question according to the translation I received, does not have any meaning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you to answer the question -- to respond to the question, but if there's a translation problem. My question simply was, when Din Krasniqi visited Jabllanice and was allowed to call himself the commander of the Barane valley, my question is, and perhaps more specific: Who then in Jabllanice allowed him to call himself the commander of the Barane valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, now I am clear about the question. Din was an educated person who was well-loved by the people in the area. He was a doctor, and in order to have no misunderstanding, the Barane valley did not have an army. But Din was well-known in the area. He had cured and treated children and the elderly, et cetera. And because the Serbs were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. My question was not why he was allowed, but who allowed him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I, myself, said that he can be commander of the area because he's well-loved by the people. He's an educated person, and nobody objected to this idea, neither Lahi nor anybody else. I proposed him to be a commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said neither Lahi. Was Lahi asked about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Din himself had insisted that I become a commander. Lahi and the others had nothing against me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please listen carefully to my questions and answer the questions. My last question was whether Lahi was asked about Din Krasniqi calling himself the commander of the Barane valley.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were discussing together, yes, of course he was asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you then when he went to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we went there together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You went there together. Why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was some fighting going on there in the Suka e Cermjanit and there were some wounded soldiers. So we went there so that Din could offer them first aid and treat them, and that's when we got to discuss about this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I take you to paragraph 41, which, Mr. Re, a bit to my surprise we have doubles there because the language is, to some extent, exactly the same as we find in 65. But I take you to paragraph 41 of your statement, where you explain that who was the commander of the 3rd Brigade in Barane; who was the commander of the 1st Brigade in Prapaqan; and who was the commander of the 2nd Brigade in Bardhaniq. Then you said: "All three brigades were, in principle, under Ramush Haradinaj, who was the overall commander, but these were also kind of independent because there were no regular systems of reporting on a daily basis. But in case of need or trouble, the zone commander was to be contacted." In your earlier answers, you gave me the impression that what you did put on the map and that the difference in brigades and staff headquarters, that it was all approximately the same, whereas in this part of your statement you clearly explain that although the brigades were instructed to do the job properly and that they were also kind of independent, that nevertheless, there was a structure where the brigades were under Ramush Haradinaj. Could you explain the differences in what you signed as your statement and the testimony you gave just before the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, there is no difference. In principle, it's the same statement, and I'd like to explain something about it, about the brigades and why they called them brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- we always thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment I do understand that my impression that your testimony was different from what your statement says is a wrong impression. If any of the parties would like further explanation on the brigades, they'll certainly ask you for it. And if at the very end of your testimony no one has asked anything about it and you consider it necessary to add anything to your testimony, you're free to do so. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the document P352 still on the screen? Could it please be put back on the screen. I just wish to pick up on Judge Hoepfel's question to the witness in relation to the writing on the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All I want you to do, Mr. Krasniqi, is just to read what it says, no comment, just read what it says.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: These three lines, as I already said: Commander of the staff is Ramush Haradinaj, deputy or operative commander was Sali Veseli, and together with him was Rrustem Tetaj. This was done --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: -- I think in June and we tried --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, no. I just asked you to read. Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I did read them, so Ramush, commander of the staff; Sali Veseli, operative commander; Rrustem Tetaj, deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that a legend for the map you've drawn there?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, is that consistent with the statement you signed today, paragraph 41, which His Honour Judge Orie's just pointed you to where you said: "The overall commander of the Dukagjini Operational Zone was Ramush Haradinaj who had his commanders" - sorry - "had his headquarters in the village Gllogjan. Sali Veseli was the operations commander for the DOZ while Rrustem Tetaj was the deputy commander." All I'm asking you is, the legend on the map, is that consistent with paragraph 41 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it is consistent with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, if I could take you to paragraph 31 of your statement in front of you there, that's your 92 ter statement you signed today, and you referred to a map which is attached as annex A to your statement of the 5th of March, 2006 --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And could you please display 65 ter Exhibit 1028.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While that's coming up, I'll just read what it says so we all know where we're going. It says: "From that day on I started training the UCK soldiers at first in Vranoc e Vogel near the river Lumbardh. At that time Dr. Din Krasniqi was the UCK commander for Vranoc and later for the Barane valley. There was 17 villages in the valley. I have shown them on a map marked as annexure A to my statement." Now, as the map comes up I just want you to identify, is this the area within the blue, are those the 17 villages which you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that receive an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against admission? No. Then it is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one I want to take you to is 65 ter Exhibit 1029, and if you could turn to paragraph 49 of your statement, please, Mr. Krasniqi, of today's statement and paragraph 48, just to give you the context, you referred to villages in Peje, Decan, and Klina being under KLA control and the MUP retreating to the Irzniq police station. Then you refer to regular gun battles between the Serbian forces and the UCK forces. And paragraph 49 says: "I have shown in red the Serbian forces' positions and in -- and the Serbian villages mentioned on the map as annexure B." I just want you to have a look at the map and it's referred to -- annexure B to your statement of -- paragraph -- the 5th of March, 2006, is that the diagram of the positions in March 1998, of the Serb and KLA forces?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There are more places where the Serb forces were which are not all marked here on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you just -- before going further, can you just describe, just name them --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, just before the witness answers that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's not entirely clear to me following this that the question that Mr. Re has just put summarizing the statement is an accurate description of what is in the statement. Between paragraphs 46 and 48, there is a description of certain events, and then at paragraph 49 there is a reference to this map. Mr. Re's question at page 79, line 8 reads as follows: "I just want you to have a look at the map," and is referred to your statement 5th of March, "is that a diagram of the positions in March 1998 of the Serb and KLA forces." Again, it's not clear to me that that is what the statement is indicating.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. I should have been Serb forces instead of villages, not KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. It's the dates I'm concerned about as well. I don't understand where Mr. Re derives that date in that question from the statement from.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's written on the map. It says March 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can see that those words appear on the map. It doesn't appear that the -- in the context of the statement, which was what was being put, that that is what is being described. Maybe, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sure the witness can explain it. He has the map, it's his map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not written by me, the words "March 1998." But the main road Peje-Decan-Gjakove was controlled by the Serbian forces. So the blue dots represent villages where there were a small number of KLA. Then the other marks are the Serbian villages and the Serbian forces, both military and special forces. From the February of that year, they started to control the main road Peje-Gjakove and the surrounding areas close to Peje there is Gorazhdec where lots of Serbs lived, Kerstec, there are Albanians living in Kerstec as well, but most of them were Serbs, and Vragoc. These are the villages that have been circled, while in Gremnik there were Serb forces there, there were Serb forces in Vuljak as well, in the concrete factory, and Arkan's unit was there in Vuljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just clarify, you said the other marks, just answer this. Do you mean the red marks when you said the other marks? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Those marks are the places where they were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you see the places you just referred to on that map, the other places?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll ask you to mark the map in a moment, but first of all what time-period does this map refer to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This map refers to the time-period when -- well, the question that was asked to me was: Where did the Serb population live.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm asking you now, just concentrate on this, what time-period does that map refer to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This map covers the period until the end of March. This shows the areas where Serbian forces were stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: March 1998?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, March 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The other villages you just referred to, I can't read them out, because they were not properly transcribed, that will be later, can you mark them on the map in a different colour - can we have a green or something colour, maybe in green -- no, blue is already on it. Can we have another colour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have already red and blue, so therefore -- black would do as well, but then of course, we do not know anymore the writing in black and the original print in black. Do we have any other colours than blue and red?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we need black.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It might be a different blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a different blue, Mr. Registrar? Is there a darker blue? Okay. Dark blue would do as well because the marking until now is in light blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Same exercise. You've marked in red. Just draw on the screen in blue the places where there were other Serbian positions.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Here in Gllogjan with blue colours there were members of Kosovo Liberation Army. In Irzniq, the same, Prilep. I'm not sure whether you are looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, no, I was only interested in the Serbian positions. You said there was additional Serbian positions you had not marked on the map. That's all I'm interested in at the moment.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Rakovine, Rakovic Road which leads to Klina and Gjakove, this area of Rakovine here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you mark so we can follow it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One by one, please, so we can see where it is. I see a marking now close to Rakovine. The next one would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is also the road, but that is not indicated here, the road to Ponovik -- Kramovik, yes, there is a black arrow. So Rakovine and Kramovik here as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that it?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: These were two areas. Then also the area near Gogov, Kadol [as interpreted] here, there were also here. It's the area covering the distance between Gjakove and Klina. Jabllanice, Krstovski [as interpreted] is a village in which there was a population, Decan; then on the other side of Decan, Pishtan, Jabllanice. Then Babiq, it's a village with mixed population. Then there is Doberdol. Then in Gaboc, there were few there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No more?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: There are also in other places, in Zagerme, in Bellopoje, in Strellc, Lybeniq, Libushe, this is after March. This is the highway up to Decan. The same for Carrabreg, then if you continue down to Prilep.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that is all already marked by red stripings, which I did understand is the presence of Serb forces. So I don't think that additional dark blue marking is necessary there because we find a red marking already. May I just seek one matter to be clarified. You just mentioned Jablanica. That is a Jablanica different, I take it, from the Jablanica where the headquarters were, as you said before, the Jablanica where Lahi Brahimaj was located, which is more southerly. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are two different things. There are several Jabllanice. In Peje area there are three Jabllanices. This is in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to make sure that there would be no confusion in that respect. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, this would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be P354.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no objections, I hear no objections, P354 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one is 65 ter 1030.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I refer you to paragraph 79 of your statement, which you have there -- which you signed today and while it's coming -- it comes from paragraph 74 of your statement of the 5th of March last year and it says: "One month later in July the Serbs entered Loxha and destroyed it completely. I have provided on the map the Serb positions in red and the Albanian positions in blue in the first battle of Loxha. It's annexed as annex E." When this exhibit comes up in front of you - that's 1030 - I just wanted to ask you is that in fact the map of the Serb positions in red and the Albanian positions in blue of the first battle of Loxha in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, in blue is our free area, the area where we could move. In red colours you could see the areas in which Serbian forces were deployed. And there is also Suka e Bitesh. It should have been added in the first map, in the previous map, I'm talking about. In Diga [as interpreted] Radoniq near the lake there was Serbian forces there and also in Bitesh.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you said blue is our free area, did the KLA control that area militarily?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This is how we considered at that time. We considered it was a free area. They also, the Serbian forces, could enter this area sometimes because they had the people and the vehicles. But we moved around those areas. They, the Serbs, could also move into these areas if they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that because of their greater military might, that they could move in if they wanted to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. We did not have equipment. We had young people, volunteers, without experience, we had no army, regular army, no commanding -- genuine commanding structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be number P355, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No objection to that map being received into evidence. What I am slightly concerned about is that the witness has just indicated that two locations in respect of the previous map, which he has said in his evidence should have been inserted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- on the previous map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Donji Bites, and the other one was?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And Lake Radoniq.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He said close to Lake Radoniq? Now, Donji Bites is not far from Lake Radoniq so therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Although he's indicating two different locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If perhaps in cross-examination you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy to pick it up in cross-examination but we've just admitted a map that the witness is now saying does not properly reflect his recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he was talking about the previous map instead of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not about this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the previous map was already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm in Your Honour's hands. I'll deal with it in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But certainly it is on the record now that the previous map does not reflect, in full, Serb positions and two were added orally now by the witness. If no objections, then P355 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can that please remain on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to look at that map. I'll refer you to paragraph 44 of your statement signed today where you say: "There were 40 to 50 villages in the Dukagjini Zone under the control of the KLA in March 1998." Are those 40 to 50 villages shown within that blue area on map P355?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the map of the villages. These are the villages. However, we could not have them under total control. We could not prevent everybody to enter into these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 65 ter Exhibit 1380.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a photograph now, Mr. Krasniqi. In your statement on the 17th of May you described -- sorry, signed 21st of May this year, you described this photograph as containing the house of Lahi Brahimaj in Jablanica. You said: "I have driven past it but never been inside. I don't know what it was used for in 1998." Can you circle on that map -- on that photograph the house of Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, this house here. Should I encircle?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, please, large circle.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P356, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Then P356 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Also while in Jablanica -- can you please be shown 65 ter Exhibit 1357, which is a photograph. At paragraph 21 of your statement of the 21st of May, this year, you described it as building containing the Jablanica KLA staff in 1998 and you said you have been to this building. I just want you to identify if that's the building you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the place I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence, too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is -- I just wonder whether this is not yet in evidence. It looks very familiar. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think it might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you would say for the Chamber to find out whether it is already.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it may have been introduced during the testimony of Witness 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you please assign a number to it, but it may be that the number will be vacated at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we'll mark this for identification as P357.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown 65 ter Exhibit 1379.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your statement, paragraph 21 of May 2007 you described it as showing a building of the Jablanica KLA staff compound, and to your knowledge it was used as a kitchen. You saw cooks with food for the KLA soldiers coming in and out of this building. "I never entered the building and I do not know if people were detained there," but you heard, "from my soldiers that KLA soldiers who had sold KLA weapons were interrogated there." Is that the building you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is the building when I went there I saw the cook giving bread to some soldiers. That was normal thing to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but this -- I'm sure that this one is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have just been informed by my case manager that it doesn't have an exhibit number. I'm relying on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At the same time, I remember a person looking into the cellar where we heard quite some evidence that there was water in the cellar. So unless at two different moments different pictures were taken of this same house, there's no doubt about that, with a person in a light suit almost on his knees at exactly that same place, then please verify first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: Before Mr. Re goes any further, can I just draw the Court's attention to paragraph 21. I believe Mr. Re said that the statement read that the soldiers were detained there. In actual fact, the statement as written says: "I heard from my soldiers that KLA soldiers who had sold KLA weapons were interrogated there."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If I said that, I misspoke, I misread it, but definitely see it now. It says --

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: It's a quite significant difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise if I said -- it's entirely innocent. I heard -- it says: "I heard from KLA -- from my soldiers the KLA soldiers who had sold KLA weapons were interrogated there." I take that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TROOP
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's now corrected on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Were you referring to the statement of 15th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, 15th of May, 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we always have to choose among four statements at this moment to find out where we are. Okay. That's the 15th of May. It has been corrected. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We can't find an exhibit number for this, but I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, photograph D35, can that please be shown to you. It's an overhead photograph of the village of Gllogjan, and I refer you to -- for the Chamber's benefit paragraph 20 of the statement of May this year in which you say that it's a photograph of the village of Gllogjan, Haradinaj family house is in the photograph. It is the big house at the right side of the road when coming from Dubrava. That is the house I went to three times in 1998 and where I met Ramush Haradinaj. Annexed your photograph to your statement. Can you just please when that comes up circle that photograph.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just circle the house to which you refer.

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Certainly. Even though I've never seen this place from such an angle, nevertheless I'll try. I came from this area, here, I met him here. This house should be the house used as headquarters. This is the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This marked photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P358.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Do we have 358 already?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But as I said then, I've never seen this area from this angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if we might just for absolute clarity look at the last sentence in that paragraph and invite the witness to clarify an apparent contradiction between the passage that Mr. Re has read and the last sentence, which does not appear on the face of it to be entirely consistent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it seems that the beginning of paragraph 20 and the end of paragraph 20 contradicts. He said: "This is the house where I went three times in 1998." He described that he went three times in 1998 to the headquarters in Gllogjan, and now at the very end he says: "The layout of the village has changed since 1998 and I don't recognise any house used by the KLA in 1998 at the picture."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I just want to clarify. Is that -- do you believe that to be the house where you met Mr. Haradinaj three times or that to be his -- to be something else?

utterances.speaker: CUFE KRASNIQI
utterances.text: If I was in that position and see it the way I saw it then, then it would have been easier. Now the view of the village has changed and it is difficult for me to recognise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we spend a lot of time on it, is there any dispute as this being -- because we have seen this -- this house before and it was described earlier as the place where people went if they said they went to the headquarters. Any dispute about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We think it may not be as clear as the Prosecution thinks it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there is dispute about it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I could ask him a lot more questions, but he's not -- I don't think it's going to assist --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to you, Mr. Re, whether you think it -- what you just circled, on the basis of what did you circle that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
